subject: Concord Biotech renewal: usage health, ROI recap & runbook
messages:
From: Maya Singh <maya@concordbio.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>
Cc: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@concordbio.com>, procurement@concordbio.com
Date: 2027-10-01T09:12:00Z
Subject: Renewal check — usage report attached & Q for capacity

Hi Grace,

We pulled the September spend and usage for our assistant stack and wanted to share — attaching the export (concord_usage_report_202709.pdf). A few quick notes: average token spend is ~1.9M/month, a 42% jump quarter-over-quarter after we rolled out context-window features in August. Latency has been fine, but we saw a couple of burst windows where tail latency hit ~800ms for a short period during batch inference.

Our renewal is up mid-November and the finance team asked whether we should move to a committed block or keep a flexible run-rate with burst credits. We're also interested in a short canary for your Dedicated offering to reduce per-token costs. Curious on two things from your side: 1) can you confirm expected unit economics for a modest commit + quantization (we run mixed int8/x8), and 2) do you have a recommended runbook for a staged canary (traffic %s, rollback triggers, measurement windows)?

Can we get a 30-minute working session next week to review? Evan and I are available Oct 4–6 afternoons PT.

Thanks,
Maya Singh
Head of Platform Engineering
Concord Biotech

Attachments: concord_usage_report_202709.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB)

From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Singh <maya@concordbio.com>, Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@concordbio.com>, procurement@concordbio.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-01T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Renewal check — usage report attached & Q for capacity

Maya — thanks for the report and context. I dug into the numbers you sent and summarized the key signals for the call:
- Baseline tokens: ~1.9M/mo (current prod mix)
- Recent uplift driven by longer contexts; median request length up 38%
- Tail latency spikes coincide with 3 high-concurrency windows (batch jobs) — likely opportunity for burst lane or separate batch pool

Quick answers up front:
1) Committed block + int8 quantization looks like a 20–30% token cost reduction for your workload profile, depending on model variant. We can run an A/B on a 5% traffic canary to validate quality/latency.
2) I asked Ben and Karthik to draft a concise runbook with traffic ramp, SLOs, rollback triggers, and expected ROI.

Propose 30 minutes on Oct 5 at 10:30 PT — does that work for you? If procurement is ready, we can also discuss the amendment path (short addendum for burst credits + a 12-month commit).

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Customer Success — Renewals
Redwood Inference

Attachments: —

On 2027-10-01 09:12, Maya Singh wrote:
> Hi Grace,
> ... (see attached)

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-02T08:27:00Z
Subject: Draft runbook + suggested commit sizing for Concord (internal)

Grace / Karthik / Monica — attaching the runbook draft (redwood_runbook_concord_v1.xlsx). Highlights:
- Canary plan: 5% traffic for 72 hours -> 20% for 7 days -> 50% for 14 days. Measure: token cost per successful response, p95 latency, and quality checks on 500 sampled prompts.
- Rollback triggers: p95 latency > 600ms sustained for 30m, error rate increase > 0.5% absolute, or quality regression flagged by >5% of sampled prompts.
- Commit recommendation: incremental 25% commit over current run-rate (equates to ~2.4M tokens/mo committed) with a 12-month term. Estimated blended savings ~23% vs. on-demand after int8 quantization and prefetch caching.
- ROI: Year 1 projected savings ~$72k; Year 2 with adoption uplift ~$180k.

Two notes: 1) we'll need Concord's acceptance on the measurement set (Ben can share sample prompts), and 2) procurement flow requires a signed addendum for burst lanes — I included the DocuSign stub we use.

Ben

Attachments: redwood_runbook_concord_v1.xlsx (Excel, 120KB)

From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Singh <maya@concordbio.com>, Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@concordbio.com>, procurement@concordbio.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-04T15:10:00Z
Subject: Proposed canary & amendment draft (Concord)

Hi Maya / Evan —

Thanks for the patience. Ben's attached runbook is our proposed operational plan for the canary and the proposed commercial amendment (DocuSign stub attached as well). TL;DR of the proposal:
- Start: Oct 12 — 5% traffic canary for 72 hours; if green, ramp to 20% for 7 days; then 50% for 14 days. Full cutover contingent on quality stability.
- Commercial: 12-month commit at ~2.4M tokens/mo (25% above current run-rate) + 10% burst lane for unexpected batch jobs.
- Measurement: we'll use the shared sample prompt set (Ben will push) and track p95 latency, error rate, and a small human-in-the-loop quality sample.

If you approve the plan, procurement@concordbio.com can expect a DocuSign link this week to begin the amendment signature — we'll mark the amendment effective on the canary start date so you get committed pricing retroactive to ramp.

Can you confirm: 1) Oct 12 start date works, and 2) procurement is willing to accept the amendment flow via DocuSign?

Thanks,
Grace

On 2027-10-02 08:27, Ben Carter wrote:
> Grace / Karthik / Monica — attaching the runbook draft...

From: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@concordbio.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>, Maya Singh <maya@concordbio.com>, procurement@concordbio.com
Date: 2027-10-05T10:21:00Z
Subject: Re: Proposed canary & amendment draft (Concord)

Grace — thanks, this looks sensible. A couple of quick asks from our side before we pull procurement in:
1) Can you share a 1-slide ROI summary for our CFO (savings vs incremental commit + expected payback period)?
2) Can you call out the specific model variants and quant lanes (we're currently on rwd-xl and experimenting with rwd-quant8) so our ML team can vet quality risk?

Procurement: we can accept DocuSign but need the amendment routed to our legal first for a quick redline (2 business days).

If those two asks are addressed, Oct 12 start looks good.

—Evan

Attachments: —

> ... (see runbook)

From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@concordbio.com>, Maya Singh <maya@concordbio.com>, procurement@concordbio.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-07T16:04:00Z
Subject: Re: Proposed canary & amendment draft (Concord) — next steps

Evan / Maya — quick update and next steps before the canary: 

1) ROI slide: attached (one-slide summary) — shows Year 1 savings ~$72k and payback within ~4 months at the projected ramp.
2) Model lanes: we'll run canary on rwd-xl (baseline) vs rwd-quant8 (canary lane). Ben's runbook includes the exact sampling and quality checks; our recommendation is to keep human review on the 500-sample set through the 20% ramp.
3) Legal/procurement: Grace to Ben — please send the DocuSign amendment (docusign_concord_amendment.pdf) to procurement@concordbio.com with a note for legal review. We will label the amendment to start on Oct 12 so committed pricing applies from day 1 of canary ramp.

I've scheduled the kickoff meeting for Oct 11 at 10:30 PT to finalize the sample set and measurement dashboard. Invites sent separately.

If all good, Procurement can expect the DocuSign link today; we'll treat legal redlines as 2 business days.

Thanks — looking forward to a smooth canary.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Customer Success — Renewals
Redwood Inference

Attachments: concord_roi_one_slide.pdf (PDF, 45KB), docusign_concord_amendment.pdf (PDF, 12KB)
